question: A company runs its machine learning workloads on Amazon SageMaker. An ML engineer receives a 50-MB Apache Parquet file to train a fraud detection model. The dataset contains several unnecessary, correlated columns. The engineer wants to remove these columns with the least amount of effort. Which solution should the engineer use?

options.A: Create a data flow in SageMaker Data Wrangler to remove the unwanted columns
options.B: Run a custom Apache Spark job on Amazon EMR to process the Parquet file
options.C: Download the dataset to a local workstation and manually clean the data
options.D: Use a custom Python script to apply one-hot encoding to the dataset
options.E: Create a SageMaker Processing job using the SageMaker Python SDK

radar.signal: Petit fichier + nettoyage simple (drop colonnes) + effort minimal -> SageMaker Data Wrangler (no-code visuel), pas de code custom ni de cluster

pieges.B: EMR + Spark = infrastructure a gerer pour un fichier de 50 MB, largement disproportionne
pieges.C: Manuel/local = pas scalable, pas reproductible, contraire a 'least effort'
pieges.D: One-hot encoding ne supprime pas des colonnes, ce n'est pas la bonne operation
pieges.E: Processing job avec le SDK = il faut ecrire un script, plus d'effort qu'un data flow visuel Data Wrangler

explication: Pour un nettoyage simple (supprimer des colonnes correlees) sur un petit fichier, Data Wrangler offre une transformation 'Drop column' en quelques clics dans une interface visuelle, sans ecrire de code ni provisionner d'infrastructure. C'est la solution qui minimise l'effort d'ingenierie, contrairement a EMR/Spark (trop lourd), au nettoyage manuel (non reproductible) ou a un Processing job custom (necessite du code).
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: A financial services company uses Amazon SageMaker to deploy a machine learning model that evaluates loan risk for personal loan approvals. The model currently gives more importance to credit score than income. The company wants to monitor whether this feature prioritization changes over time. Which SageMaker Model Monitor component should be used to meet this requirement?

options.A: ModelQualityMonitor
options.B: ModelExplainabilityMonitor
options.C: DataQualityMonitor
options.D: ModelBiasMonitor

radar.signal: Surveiller la derive de l'importance/attribution des features dans le temps -> ModelExplainabilityMonitor (Clarify feature attribution drift)

pieges.A: ModelQualityMonitor surveille la performance du modele (accuracy, precision...), pas l'importance des features
pieges.C: DataQualityMonitor surveille la derive statistique des donnees d'entree, pas l'attribution des features au modele
pieges.D: ModelBiasMonitor detecte les biais vis-a-vis de groupes proteges, pas le classement d'importance des features

explication: Le ModelExplainabilityMonitor de SageMaker Model Monitor (base sur SageMaker Clarify) calcule periodiquement les valeurs d'attribution des features (ex: SHAP) et alerte en cas de derive de leur importance relative. C'est exactement ce qu'il faut pour verifier que la priorite donnee au credit score par rapport au revenu ne change pas dans le temps.
domain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions

question: A healthcare organization is developing an AI application on Amazon SageMaker to predict patient readmission rates. The solution must support end-to-end ML workflows, including data preprocessing, model training, versioning, and deployment. Training data is stored securely in Amazon S3 and must be processed in isolated, secure environments to meet regulatory requirements. During experimentation, the data science team runs multiple training jobs sequentially to test different hyperparameter configurations. To improve productivity, the company wants to reduce the startup time for each subsequent training job. Which solution is the MOST efficient?

options.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Managed Spot Training to speed up resource provisioning
options.B: Enable SageMaker Training Compiler to reduce training execution time
options.C: Use Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances with custom preconfigured AMIs
options.D: Enable SageMaker Warm Pools to reuse training instances across jobs

radar.signal: Jobs sequentiels + reduire le temps de demarrage entre jobs -> SageMaker Managed Warm Pools (garde l'instance 'chaude')

pieges.A: Spot Training reduit le cout, pas le temps de provisioning ; peut meme l'augmenter (attente de capacite Spot)
pieges.B: Training Compiler accelere l'execution du training, pas le demarrage/provisioning de l'infrastructure
pieges.C: Sortir de SageMaker pour EC2 custom = plus d'effort operationnel et perte des benefices manages de SageMaker

explication: SageMaker Managed Warm Pools garde l'infrastructure de training provisionnee pendant une duree configurable apres la fin d'un job, afin que le job suivant demarre quasi instantanement au lieu de re-provisionner des instances. C'est la fonctionnalite concue specifiquement pour reduire le startup time entre jobs sequentiels d'experimentation.
domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows

question: In machine learning, what does feature engineering refer to, and why is it important?

options.A: The process of adjusting hyperparameters to optimize a model's performance
options.B: The activity of visualizing datasets to identify trends and patterns
options.C: The practice of selecting, transforming, or creating features from raw data to improve model performance
options.D: The task of collecting raw data to ensure sufficient input for training models

radar.signal: Question de definition pure -> feature engineering = selectionner/transformer/creer des features a partir des donnees brutes

pieges.A: C'est la definition du hyperparameter tuning, pas du feature engineering
pieges.B: C'est de la data visualization / EDA, une etape distincte
pieges.D: C'est de la data collection, une etape en amont du feature engineering

explication: Le feature engineering consiste a selectionner, transformer ou creer des variables (features) a partir des donnees brutes afin d'ameliorer la capacite du modele a apprendre des patterns pertinents, ce qui impacte directement la performance predictive.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: A DevOps engineer manages a serverless machine learning application that delivers real-time predictions using AWS Lambda. Users are experiencing increased latency, particularly during peak traffic periods. The engineer needs to quickly identify the root cause and resolve the performance issue to keep the application responsive. Which combination of monitoring and observability tools is the MOST effective for troubleshooting this latency?

options.A: Set Amazon CloudWatch Alarms for Lambda duration and error rates, and enable periodic AWS X-Ray sampling
options.B: Use AWS X-Ray for end-to-end request tracing and combine it with Amazon CloudWatch Lambda Insights
options.C: Analyze logs using CloudWatch Logs Insights and review infrastructure changes with AWS Config
options.D: Enable detailed Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Lambda and manually review the function code for performance issues

radar.signal: Latence Lambda a identifier finement -> X-Ray (tracing bout-en-bout) + CloudWatch Lambda Insights (metriques systeme par invocation, cold starts, memoire/CPU)

pieges.A: X-Ray en 'sampling periodique' est moins precis qu'un tracing complet pour du troubleshooting cible
pieges.C: AWS Config suit les changements de configuration de ressources, pas la latence applicative
pieges.D: Revue manuelle du code = lent et pas cible par les donnees d'observabilite

explication: AWS X-Ray permet de tracer une requete de bout en bout (API Gateway -> Lambda -> services avals) pour localiser precisement ou se situe la latence, tandis que CloudWatch Lambda Insights fournit des metriques systeme detaillees par invocation (duree, memoire, CPU, cold starts). La combinaison des deux est l'approche la plus efficace pour diagnostiquer rapidement un probleme de latence en pic de charge.
domain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions

question: In Amazon SageMaker Clarify, which type of metrics are used to detect potential bias in training data by comparing feature distributions across different groups?

options.A: Model Accuracy Metrics
options.B: Data Bias Metrics
options.C: Feature Importance Metrics
options.D: Data Quality Metrics

radar.signal: Biais DANS les DONNEES (pre-training), comparaison de distributions entre groupes -> Data Bias Metrics de Clarify

pieges.A: Model Accuracy Metrics mesurent la performance du modele, pas un biais dans les donnees
pieges.C: Feature Importance Metrics mesurent la contribution des features aux predictions, pas la distribution par groupe
pieges.D: Data Quality Metrics couvrent des problemes comme les valeurs manquantes/outliers, pas specifiquement le biais entre groupes

explication: SageMaker Clarify calcule des metriques de biais pre-entrainement ('Data Bias Metrics', ex: Class Imbalance, Difference in Proportions of Labels) qui comparent les distributions de features/labels entre groupes sensibles afin de detecter un biais potentiel avant meme d'entrainer le modele.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: A publishing company wants to automatically identify and extract meaningful, unique keywords from a large set of documents using AWS services. Which solution allows the ML engineer to achieve this with minimal operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon Comprehend with custom entity recognition and key phrase extraction
options.B: Use Amazon Textract to extract entities and key phrases from documents
options.C: Use Amazon Rekognition to detect entities and key phrases in the documents
options.D: Use Amazon Kendra to search and extract meaningful, unique keywords

radar.signal: Extraction de mots-cles/phrases dans du texte -> Amazon Comprehend (DetectKeyPhrases, service manage NLP)

pieges.B: Textract est un service d'OCR/extraction de formulaires, pas de key phrase extraction linguistique
pieges.C: Rekognition analyse des images/videos, pas du texte
pieges.D: Kendra est un moteur de recherche d'entreprise, pas un outil d'extraction de mots-cles

explication: Amazon Comprehend est le service NLP manage d'AWS capable d'extraire automatiquement des key phrases (et des entites) d'un texte via une simple API, sans entrainement ni infrastructure a gerer, ce qui correspond au besoin d'overhead operationnel minimal. Textract, Rekognition et Kendra ne sont pas concus pour cette tache d'extraction linguistique de mots-cles.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: A healthcare organization is building a deep learning model on Amazon SageMaker to predict patient outcomes. The training dataset is large, and the goal is to optimize hyperparameters to minimize the loss on the validation dataset. Which hyperparameter tuning strategy should the organization choose to achieve this with the least computational effort?

options.A: Grid search
options.B: Hyperband
options.C: Random Forest
options.D: Gradient descent

radar.signal: Dataset volumineux + minimiser le cout de calcul du HPO -> Hyperband (arret precoce des configurations peu prometteuses)

pieges.A: Grid search teste exhaustivement toutes les combinaisons -> tres couteux en calcul
pieges.C: Random Forest est un algorithme de modele, pas une strategie de tuning d'hyperparametres
pieges.D: Gradient descent optimise les poids du modele pendant l'entrainement, ce n'est pas une strategie de recherche d'hyperparametres

explication: La strategie Hyperband (supportee nativement par SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning) utilise l'arret precoce des essais peu performants pour concentrer les ressources de calcul sur les configurations prometteuses, ce qui reduit fortement le cout de calcul par rapport au grid search exhaustif, particulierement utile sur un large dataset.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: A company uses an ML model to generate text descriptions for product images uploaded by customers. Each image can be up to 40 MB. To cost-effectively handle inference requests while scaling with demand, images are stored in Amazon S3. Which solution provides scalable, low-overhead processing for these inference requests?

options.A: Create an Amazon SageMaker Real-Time Inference endpoint and trigger a Lambda function for each image upload
options.B: Use SageMaker Batch Transform to process the images stored in S3 in bulk
options.C: Create a SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint and run a script to invoke it for each image
options.D: Create an Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint with a scaling policy and trigger a Lambda function for each image

radar.signal: Payload volumineux (jusqu'a 40 MB) + demande variable -> SageMaker Asynchronous Inference (payloads jusqu'a 1 GB, scale-to-zero)

pieges.A: Real-Time Inference limite la taille de payload a 6 MB, insuffisant pour des images de 40 MB, et ne scale pas a zero
pieges.B: Batch Transform convient au traitement en masse differe, pas a des requetes d'inference declenchees a l'upload
pieges.C: Serverless Inference limite le payload a 4 MB, insuffisant pour des images de 40 MB

explication: SageMaker Asynchronous Inference accepte des payloads jusqu'a 1 GB (contre 6 MB en temps reel et 4 MB en serverless), met en file les requetes et peut scaler jusqu'a zero instance en l'absence de trafic, ce qui correspond exactement au besoin de traiter des images volumineuses de maniere scalable et economique face a une demande variable.
domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows

question: In machine learning, what does the bias versus variance trade-off refer to, and why is it important for model performance?

options.A: It is a technique to improve model performance by increasing both bias and variance simultaneously
options.B: It refers to balancing errors due to model assumptions (bias) and model complexity (variance), where high bias causes underfitting and high variance causes overfitting
options.C: It involves choosing between a high-complexity model that may capture noise (high bias) and a simpler model that may generalize better (high variance)
options.D: It is the balance between underfitting and overfitting, where high bias leads to overfitting and high variance leads to underfitting

radar.signal: Question de definition -> high bias = underfitting, high variance = overfitting

pieges.A: Augmenter bias ET variance simultanement n'ameliore pas la performance, c'est absurde
pieges.C: Inverse les definitions : un modele complexe qui capture le bruit a une variance elevee, pas un bias eleve
pieges.D: Inverse aussi les associations : bias eleve -> underfitting (pas overfitting), variance elevee -> overfitting (pas underfitting)

explication: Le compromis biais-variance oppose l'erreur due a des hypotheses trop simplistes du modele (biais eleve -> sous-apprentissage/underfitting) a l'erreur due a une sensibilite excessive aux donnees d'entrainement (variance elevee -> surapprentissage/overfitting). Trouver le bon equilibre est essentiel pour maximiser la generalisation du modele.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: An organization needs a scalable solution to preprocess and transform large datasets for machine learning. The data comes from multiple sources and requires distributed processing. Which solution best meets these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to label and preprocess the data
options.B: Use Amazon EMR integrated with SageMaker Studio for distributed data processing
options.C: Use Data Wrangler within Amazon SageMaker Canvas to clean and transform the data
options.D: Use the built-in SQL extension in SageMaker Studio for preprocessing

radar.signal: Volume important + traitement distribue explicitement demande -> Amazon EMR (Spark/Hadoop) integre a SageMaker Studio

pieges.A: Ground Truth sert au labelling de donnees, pas au preprocessing distribue a grande echelle
pieges.C: Data Wrangler est adapte a des volumes moderes, pas concu comme un moteur de traitement distribue massif
pieges.D: L'extension SQL de Studio interroge des donnees, elle ne fournit pas un moteur de calcul distribue

explication: Amazon EMR fournit un moteur de traitement distribue (Spark/Hive/Hadoop) capable de scaler horizontalement sur de tres larges volumes issus de sources multiples, et son integration native avec SageMaker Studio permet d'orchestrer ce preprocessing directement dans le workflow ML, ce qui en fait la solution la plus adaptee ici.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: A customer service organization has historical data about clients who required extended support. The organization wants to build an ML model to predict whether future clients will need long-term support. Which approach is most suitable for this predictive task?

options.A: Linear Regression
options.B: Anomaly Detection
options.C: Logistic Regression
options.D: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)

radar.signal: Predire un resultat binaire (besoin ou non de support long terme) -> classification -> Logistic Regression

pieges.A: Linear Regression predit une valeur continue, pas une classe binaire
pieges.B: Anomaly Detection identifie des observations atypiques, ce n'est pas une prediction supervisee binaire
pieges.D: PCA est une technique de reduction de dimensionnalite, pas un algorithme de prediction

explication: La question demande de predire une variable binaire ('aura besoin ou non de support prolonge') a partir de donnees historiques etiquetees : c'est un probleme de classification binaire supervisee, pour lequel la regression logistique est l'approche standard et la plus adaptee parmi les options proposees.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: A Machine Learning Specialist needs to store large, time-based training data for a new model. New files arrive hourly, and the volume of updates fluctuates throughout the day. The model should always train on the last 24 hours of data. Which data repository is the most cost-effective solution?

options.A: Amazon S3 data lake using hourly object prefixes
options.B: Amazon RDS with hourly table partitions
options.C: Amazon EMR cluster with hourly Hive partitions on EBS volumes
options.D: Amazon EBS-backed EC2 instance with hourly directories

radar.signal: Stockage volumineux, horodate, volumetrie variable, cout minimal -> S3 avec prefixes horaires (data lake)

pieges.B: RDS = base relationnelle geree, couteuse et non concue pour de gros volumes de fichiers bruts
pieges.C: Cluster EMR + EBS = infrastructure active en permanence, cout et overhead bien plus eleves qu'un simple stockage S3
pieges.D: EC2+EBS = paye pour du compute/stockage bloc en continu, alors qu'aucun traitement n'est requis ici, juste du stockage

explication: Amazon S3 est le stockage objet le moins cher a grande echelle, elastique face aux fluctuations de volume, et l'organisation en prefixes horaires (ex: /yyyy/mm/dd/hh/) permet de facilement selectionner uniquement les dernieres 24 heures de donnees pour l'entrainement, sans payer pour de l'infrastructure de calcul ou de base de donnees inutilisee en continu.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: A company receives about 25,000 product reviews per day into an S3 bucket, with new files arriving roughly every 10 minutes. The team wants to use Amazon Comprehend to detect sentiment and requires a workflow that, Triggers automatically when objects arrive, Minimizes custom code for loading data into Comprehend, Supports a reliable continuous deployment pipeline for updates. Which AWS services should be used with Amazon Comprehend to meet these requirements?

options.A: AWS Lambda, AWS CodePipeline, and Amazon S3
options.B: AWS Step Functions, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon S3
options.C: Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS, and Amazon SQS
options.D: Amazon ECS, AWS Batch, and Amazon DynamoDB

radar.signal: S3 event -> Lambda (peu de code) + CodePipeline explicitement pour le CI/CD des mises a jour

pieges.B: Step Functions + EventBridge ajoutent de l'orchestration mais ne repondent pas directement au besoin explicite de pipeline de deploiement continu
pieges.C: EC2/RDS/SQS = architecture a gerer soi-meme, ni evenementielle nativement ni faible en code
pieges.D: ECS/Batch/DynamoDB visent un traitement par lots gere, pas un declenchement immediat a l'arrivee de chaque fichier

explication: Un declencheur S3 sur AWS Lambda permet d'appeler l'API Comprehend DetectSentiment automatiquement des qu'un fichier arrive, avec un minimum de code. AWS CodePipeline repond precisement a l'exigence d'un pipeline de deploiement continu fiable pour faire evoluer ce code. C'est la seule option qui couvre les trois exigences simultanement.
domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows

question: A manufacturing company wants to build an anomaly detection system to identify defective products on its production lines. The datasets include, Sensor logs from IoT devices stored in Amazon S3, Production metadata from an on-premises SQL database. Requirements, Aggregate and preprocess data from multiple sources. Automatically detect anomalies in sensor data. Visualize results for the operations team. Which solution meets these requirements most efficiently?

options.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to aggregate, clean, and prepare data for anomaly detection while generating visual insights
options.B: Use Amazon EMR with Spark MLlib to run anomaly detection and visualize results with custom dashboards
options.C: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for real-time sensor analysis and Amazon QuickSight for visualization
options.D: Use Amazon Athena to query sensor data and detect anomalies with SQL, then Amazon QuickSight to visualize

radar.signal: Sources multiples (S3 + SQL on-prem via JDBC) + agregation + insights visuels en un seul outil -> SageMaker Data Wrangler

pieges.B: EMR + MLlib + dashboards custom = solution la plus lourde a construire et a maintenir, contraire a 'most efficiently'
pieges.C: Kinesis Data Streams ne se connecte pas nativement a une base SQL on-premises et ne fait pas d'agregation multi-source
pieges.D: Athena interroge des donnees dans S3/Glue Catalog, pas directement une base SQL on-premises ; detection d'anomalies via SQL brut est peu fiable

explication: SageMaker Data Wrangler peut se connecter a de multiples sources (S3, et bases relationnelles via connecteur JDBC pour une base on-premises), agreger et nettoyer les donnees, et generer des insights/visualisations directement dans son interface, offrant la solution la plus integree et la moins couteuse en effort pour repondre aux trois exigences en une seule fois.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: Which of the following are examples of supervised learning? (Choose two)

options.A: Clustering
options.B: Document Classification
options.C: Linear Regression
options.D: Neural Network
options.E: Association Rule Learning

radar.signal: Chercher les taches avec labels connus -> classification et regression sont les exemples canoniques d'apprentissage supervise

pieges.A: Le clustering est une technique non supervisee (pas de labels)
pieges.D: Un reseau de neurones est une architecture de modele, utilisable en supervise comme en non supervise -> pas un exemple univoque
pieges.E: L'association rule learning (ex: panier d'achat) est une technique non supervisee

explication: La classification de documents et la regression lineaire sont deux taches classiques d'apprentissage supervise : elles s'entrainent sur des donnees etiquetees (label connu) pour predire une categorie ou une valeur. Le clustering et l'association rule learning sont non supervises, et 'Neural Network' designe une architecture, pas un paradigme d'apprentissage en soi.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: Which statement correctly describes techniques used to improve the performance of a Foundation Model (FM)?

options.A: Both Fine-tuning and RAG change the weights of the FM
options.B: Neither Fine-tuning nor RAG changes the weights of the FM
options.C: Fine-tuning changes the weights of the FM, whereas Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) does not change the weights
options.D: Fine-tuning does not change the weights of the FM, whereas RAG changes the weights

radar.signal: Fine-tuning = ré-entrainement -> modifie les poids ; RAG = injection de contexte externe au prompt -> ne modifie pas les poids

pieges.A: RAG ne fait qu'enrichir le prompt avec du contexte recupere, il ne re-entraine pas le modele
pieges.B: Le fine-tuning, lui, met bien a jour les poids du modele via un entrainement supplementaire
pieges.D: Inverse totalement les deux techniques

explication: Le fine-tuning consiste a poursuivre l'entrainement du Foundation Model sur des donnees specifiques, ce qui modifie ses poids. Le RAG, lui, recupere des informations pertinentes (ex: depuis une base vectorielle) et les injecte dans le prompt au moment de l'inference, sans jamais toucher aux poids du modele.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: A company is building a web-based AI application using Amazon SageMaker that includes ML experimentation, training, a model registry, deployment, and monitoring. The training data is stored in Amazon S3, and the company runs multiple consecutive training jobs. The solution must ensure secure and isolated training environments. How can the company minimize infrastructure startup times for these consecutive training jobs?

options.A: Use SageMaker Training Compiler to optimize training execution
options.B: Use SageMaker managed warm pools to keep training instances ready
options.C: Use SageMaker Distributed Data Parallel (SMDDP) for faster distributed training
options.D: Use Managed Spot Training to reduce training cost

radar.signal: Meme pattern que le warm-up de jobs sequentiels -> SageMaker Managed Warm Pools

pieges.A: Training Compiler optimise la vitesse d'execution du training, pas le temps de demarrage de l'infra
pieges.C: SMDDP accelere l'entrainement distribue, sans rapport avec le temps de provisioning
pieges.D: Spot Training vise le cout, pas la reduction du temps de demarrage (et peut meme le degrader)

explication: Comme pour un scenario equivalent, la fonctionnalite Managed Warm Pools de SageMaker maintient les instances de training provisionnees entre deux jobs consecutifs, eliminant le delai de provisioning et reduisant ainsi le temps de demarrage global du workflow d'entrainement iteratif.
domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows

question: A data scientist is using AWS Glue DataBrew to prepare data for a customer churn prediction model. Which task is most likely to be performed in DataBrew?

options.A: Cleaning and transforming customer data
options.B: Building a machine learning model
options.C: Identifying customer segments
options.D: Evaluating the model's performance

radar.signal: DataBrew = outil visuel de data preparation (nettoyage/transformation), pas un outil de modelisation

pieges.B: DataBrew ne construit pas de modeles ML, ce role revient a SageMaker
pieges.C: La segmentation client est une tache de modelisation (clustering), hors perimetre de DataBrew
pieges.D: L'evaluation de modele se fait dans SageMaker (ou autre outil ML), pas dans DataBrew

explication: AWS Glue DataBrew est un outil visuel de preparation de donnees (nettoyage, normalisation, transformation) sans code. Son role dans un projet ML se limite a preparer le jeu de donnees en amont ; la construction et l'evaluation du modele relevent d'autres services comme SageMaker.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: You are evaluating a text summarization model on tasks involving long documents. To measure the semantic similarity between the generated summaries and the original text, which evaluation metric is most appropriate?

options.A: ROUGE
options.B: BERTScore
options.C: BLEU
options.D: Perplexity

radar.signal: Similarite SEMANTIQUE (sens) plutot que chevauchement de mots -> BERTScore (embeddings contextuels)

pieges.A: ROUGE mesure le recouvrement de n-grammes (lexical), pas la similarite semantique
pieges.C: BLEU mesure aussi un chevauchement de n-grammes (surtout utilise en traduction), pas le sens
pieges.D: La perplexite mesure la fluence/probabilite du texte genere par un modele de langage, pas sa similarite a une reference

explication: BERTScore compare des embeddings contextuels (issus d'un modele type BERT) entre le texte genere et la reference, capturant ainsi la similarite de sens meme en l'absence de chevauchement exact de mots, contrairement a ROUGE et BLEU qui restent des metriques purement lexicales base sur le comptage de n-grammes.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: A company has tabular training datasets on Amazon S3 with millions of rows. They need to prepare the data for ML jobs, including selection, cleansing, exploration, and visualization, using a single visual interface. Which Amazon SageMaker service is best suited for this task?

options.A: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store
options.B: Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler
options.C: Amazon SageMaker Clarify
options.D: SageMaker Model Dashboard

radar.signal: Selection + nettoyage + exploration + visualisation en UNE interface visuelle -> SageMaker Data Wrangler

pieges.A: Feature Store stocke et sert des features deja calculees, il ne les nettoie/explore pas
pieges.C: Clarify se concentre sur le biais et l'explicabilite, pas sur la preparation generale de donnees
pieges.D: Model Dashboard suit les modeles deployes en production, sans rapport avec la data prep

explication: SageMaker Data Wrangler est concu precisement pour couvrir en une seule interface visuelle toutes les etapes citees : selection de colonnes, nettoyage, exploration statistique et visualisation, avant export vers un job d'entrainement, ce qui en fait le service le plus adapte parmi les options proposees.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: You are preparing a dataset for machine learning using SageMaker Data Wrangler. The dataset contains numeric columns with missing values. To ensure optimal model performance, you need to replace missing values in each numeric column with the column mean. Which Data Wrangler transformation should you use?

options.A: Scale
options.B: Drop
options.C: Impute
options.D: Encode

radar.signal: Remplacer des valeurs manquantes par une statistique (moyenne) -> transformation 'Impute'

pieges.A: Scale normalise l'echelle des valeurs numeriques, ne traite pas les valeurs manquantes
pieges.B: Drop supprimerait la colonne ou la ligne, on perdrait des donnees au lieu de les completer
pieges.D: Encode convertit des categories en valeurs numeriques, sans rapport avec les valeurs manquantes

explication: Dans SageMaker Data Wrangler, la transformation 'Impute' permet de remplacer les valeurs manquantes d'une colonne numerique par une statistique choisie (par exemple la moyenne), ce qui correspond exactement au besoin decrit, contrairement a Scale, Drop ou Encode qui remplissent d'autres roles.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: A Machine Learning Specialist needs to query a dataset on Amazon S3 using Amazon Athena. The dataset contains, 800,000+ records stored as plaintext CSV. Each record has 200 columns and is ~1.5 MB in size. Most queries use only 5-10 columns. Which transformation will minimize query runtime?

options.A: Convert the dataset to JSON
options.B: Convert the dataset to Apache Parquet
options.C: Convert the dataset to GZIP CSV
options.D: Convert the dataset to XML

radar.signal: Beaucoup de colonnes mais seules quelques-unes sont lues par requete -> format colonnaire Parquet (Athena ne scanne que les colonnes utiles)

pieges.A: JSON reste un format ligne (row-based), voire plus volumineux et lent a parser que le CSV
pieges.C: GZIP CSV reduit la taille de stockage mais reste un format ligne : Athena doit toujours lire toutes les colonnes de chaque ligne
pieges.D: XML est encore plus verbeux qu'un CSV/JSON et reste un format ligne, donc pire en performance

explication: Apache Parquet est un format de stockage colonnaire : Athena peut alors ne scanner que les 5 a 10 colonnes reellement utilisees par les requetes au lieu des 200 colonnes completes de chaque enregistrement CSV, ce qui reduit drastiquement le volume de donnees scannees et donc le temps (et le cout) d'execution des requetes.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: A company wants to host a custom ML model for forecast analysis. Requirements, Predictable, sustained load for the same 2-hour period every day. Multiple invocations during this period require quick responses. AWS must manage infrastructure and auto scaling. Which solution meets these requirements most effectively?

options.A: Use SageMaker Serverless Inference with provisioned concurrency
options.B: Schedule a SageMaker Batch Transform job triggered by Lambda
options.C: Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling group with scheduled scaling
options.D: Deploy the model on EKS with pod auto scaling

radar.signal: Fenetre de charge previsible et recurrente + reponses rapides + AWS gere tout -> Serverless Inference avec provisioned concurrency (evite le cold start pendant la fenetre connue)

pieges.B: Batch Transform traite des lots hors-ligne, incompatible avec des reponses rapides a des invocations individuelles
pieges.C: Un Auto Scaling Group EC2 laisse le client gerer les instances/patches, contraire a 'AWS must manage infrastructure'
pieges.D: EKS impose de gerer un cluster Kubernetes, l'overhead operationnel le plus eleve des quatre options

explication: SageMaker Serverless Inference avec provisioned concurrency permet d'eliminer les cold starts pendant une fenetre de trafic connue et recurrente (les 2 heures quotidiennes), tout en laissant AWS gerer entierement l'infrastructure et la mise a l'echelle, ce qui correspond point par point aux exigences enoncees.
domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows

question: An insurtech startup is building a near-real-time claim risk model with Amazon SageMaker. They have a 72 MB Parquet dataset with multiple correlated fields that the model won't use. The goal is to remove unused columns with minimal effort while keeping the dataset ready for feature processing and training in SageMaker. Which approach is most efficient?

options.A: Write a Python script with pandas to read the Parquet, drop columns, and save back to Parquet
options.B: Create an AWS Glue ETL job to read the Parquet file and drop the unwanted columns before loading into SageMaker
options.C: Use Amazon Athena CTAS to select only the needed columns and write a new Parquet file to S3
options.D: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to load the Parquet file, remove the unused columns, and export the processed dataset

declencheurs: ready for feature processing and training in SageMaker
radar.signal: Meme pattern que Q1 : suppression de colonnes, effort minimal, rester dans l'ecosysteme SageMaker -> Data Wrangler

pieges.A: Script pandas = code custom a ecrire et maintenir, plus d'effort qu'un outil visuel
pieges.B: Glue ETL job = plus de configuration/overhead (jobs Spark, IAM, planification) pour une simple suppression de colonnes
pieges.C: Athena CTAS necessite que le dataset soit deja catalogue (Glue Data Catalog) et implique d'ecrire du SQL, une etape supplementaire

explication: Comme pour la suppression de colonnes correlees dans un petit fichier Parquet, SageMaker Data Wrangler permet de charger le fichier, appliquer une transformation visuelle 'Drop column' et exporter directement le resultat pret pour le feature processing et l'entrainement dans SageMaker, le tout sans ecrire ni maintenir de code, ce qui minimise l'effort tout en restant integre a l'ecosysteme SageMaker.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: A data scientist at a travel-booking startup needs to analyze nearly 40 TB of clickstream and purchase data stored in Parquet format on Amazon S3. The requirement is to run interactive SQL queries directly on the data, avoid data movement, and keep operational overhead as low as possible. Which approach using Amazon Athena best meets these requirements?

options.A: Transfer the Parquet files from Amazon S3 into an Amazon Redshift cluster using AWS Glue and query them through Athena
options.B: Define an Athena database and create external tables that reference the Parquet files stored in Amazon S3, then execute SQL queries in Athena
options.C: Import the S3 data into an Amazon RDS database and configure Athena to query the RDS tables
options.D: Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to query the S3 data and visualize the query results through Athena

declencheurs: interactive SQL queries directly on the data
radar.signal: Requeter des donnees deja dans S3 sans les deplacer -> Athena + tables externes pointant directement sur S3, aucun transfert

pieges.A: Transferer vers Redshift = deplacement de donnees et pipeline Glue a maintenir, contraire a 'avoid data movement'
pieges.C: RDS n'est pas concu pour interroger 40 TB de fichiers Parquet, et Athena n'interroge pas directement des tables RDS
pieges.D: Redshift Spectrum est une alternative valide mais introduit un cluster Redshift a gerer ; la question demande explicitement une approche via Athena seul

explication: Athena permet de definir des tables externes qui pointent directement sur les fichiers Parquet stockes dans S3 (via le Glue Data Catalog) et d'executer des requetes SQL sans jamais deplacer les donnees ni gerer d'infrastructure, ce qui correspond exactement aux trois exigences : requetes interactives, zero deplacement de donnees, overhead operationnel minimal.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: A retail company serves real-time product recommendations using a machine learning model hosted on an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. A new version of the model is ready, and the company wants to test it using real customer traffic without impacting the existing production model. The goal is to evaluate whether the new model performs better before promoting it to production. What is the most appropriate approach?

options.A: Deploy the new model to a separate SageMaker endpoint and build a custom mechanism to divide live traffic between the two endpoints
options.B: Enable SageMaker shadow testing to send a duplicate of live customer requests to the new model while the production model continues serving responses, then compare results
options.C: Host both models on a SageMaker multi-model endpoint and rely on log analysis to compare their prediction outputs
options.D: Update the existing SageMaker endpoint with the new model version, observe its performance in production, and roll back if problems occur

declencheurs: test it using real customer traffic
without impacting the existing production model
radar.signal: Tester un candidat sur du trafic reel SANS impacter la production -> SageMaker Shadow Testing (le modele shadow ne repond jamais au client)

pieges.A: Diviser le trafic reel = le nouveau modele impacte une partie des vrais clients, contraire a 'without impacting production'
pieges.C: Un multi-model endpoint sert les deux modeles aux clients, ce n'est pas un test isole et sans impact
pieges.D: Remplacer directement le modele de production expose tous les clients au risque avant meme validation

explication: Le Shadow Testing de SageMaker duplique silencieusement le trafic de production vers le nouveau modele (le 'shadow'), qui traite les requetes sans jamais renvoyer sa reponse au client : la production continue de servir normalement pendant que l'equipe compare les performances des deux modeles sur du trafic reel, sans aucun risque pour les utilisateurs.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: An organization needs to automatically rotate third-party API access tokens every 90 days on AWS. The solution should require minimal manual intervention while following AWS best practices for secret management. Which option best satisfies this requirement?

options.A: Store the API token in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and use a scheduled AWS Lambda function to update it
options.B: Enable AWS Secrets Manager managed rotation for generic secrets without customization
options.C: Generate temporary credentials using AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS)
options.D: Use AWS Secrets Manager with a custom AWS Lambda rotation function to handle token renewal

declencheurs: AWS best practices for secret management
radar.signal: Secret tiers (non natif AWS) a faire tourner automatiquement -> Secrets Manager + fonction Lambda de rotation CUSTOM (la rotation managee sans code ne couvre pas les secrets tiers arbitraires)

pieges.A: Parameter Store + Lambda planifie = reinvente manuellement ce que Secrets Manager fournit nativement avec son framework de rotation
pieges.B: La rotation managee 'sans customisation' de Secrets Manager cible des types de secrets AWS predefinis (RDS, Redshift...), pas un token d'API tiers arbitraire
pieges.C: AWS STS genere des credentials temporaires IAM, sans rapport avec la rotation d'un token d'API tiers

explication: AWS Secrets Manager est le service dedie a la gestion et rotation de secrets. Pour un token d'API tiers (type de secret non standard), il faut fournir une fonction Lambda de rotation personnalisee qui s'integre au framework de rotation de Secrets Manager, ce qui automatise le renouvellement tous les 90 jours tout en suivant les best practices AWS (secret jamais en clair dans le code, rotation auditee).
domain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions

question: A company uses an AWS Lambda function to track performance metrics from a machine learning model. An ML engineer must implement a solution that automatically sends an email notification whenever a metric exceeds a defined threshold. Which solution meets this requirement?

options.A: Record the metrics in AWS CloudTrail and configure a trail to trigger email notifications
options.B: Log the metrics to Amazon CloudFront and use access logs to detect threshold breaches
options.C: Publish the metrics to Amazon CloudWatch and configure a CloudWatch alarm to send an email notification
options.D: Store the metrics in AWS CloudTrail logs and monitor them using CloudWatch Events

radar.signal: Metrique + seuil + alerte email -> CloudWatch metrics + CloudWatch Alarm (integration SNS pour l'email)

pieges.A: CloudTrail journalise les appels API (audit), ce n'est pas un service de metriques numeriques avec seuils
pieges.B: CloudFront est un CDN ; ses access logs ne sont pas concus pour du suivi de metriques de modele ML
pieges.D: CloudTrail + CloudWatch Events surveille des evenements/changements, pas des seuils sur une valeur de metrique custom

explication: Amazon CloudWatch est le service natif pour publier des metriques custom (via put_metric_data) et configurer une alarme qui se declenche des qu'un seuil est franchi, alarme qui peut etre reliee a une notification Amazon SNS par email. C'est la solution standard et la plus directe pour ce besoin.
domain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions

question: A financial services organization wants to enhance its credit risk assessment model using Amazon SageMaker. The team requires AWS services that support data labeling and automated machine learning model training to reduce manual effort. Which two SageMaker services should they use? (Choose two)

options.A: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor
options.B: Amazon SageMaker Autopilot
options.C: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
options.D: Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler

radar.signal: Deux besoins distincts : labelling -> Ground Truth ; AutoML -> Autopilot

pieges.A: Model Monitor surveille un modele deja deploye, ne fait ni labelling ni entrainement
pieges.D: Data Wrangler prepare/transforme les donnees, il ne labellise pas et n'automatise pas l'entrainement

explication: SageMaker Ground Truth repond au besoin de labellisation des donnees (avec assistance humaine/automatique), tandis que SageMaker Autopilot automatise l'entrainement et le tuning de plusieurs modeles candidats (AutoML), reduisant l'effort manuel sur les deux etapes citees.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: A data science team uses Amazon SageMaker notebook instances to collaboratively build machine learning models. Team members need consistent access to shared datasets stored in specific Amazon S3 buckets. Currently, each notebook instance has its own IAM role, resulting in duplicated effort and inconsistent permissions. The company wants to centralize and simplify access management so all team notebooks have uniform S3 access. Which solution best meets this requirement?

options.A: Grant S3 access by attaching permissions directly to each data scientist's IAM user for fine-grained control
options.B: Assign inline IAM policies individually to each SageMaker notebook instance to control S3 access
options.C: Create a single IAM role with the required S3 permissions and attach it to all SageMaker notebook instances used by the team
options.D: Create an IAM group for the data science team, attach S3 access policies to the group, and associate the group with SageMaker notebook instances

declencheurs: each notebook instance has its own IAM role
radar.signal: Acces uniforme entre plusieurs notebook instances -> UN role IAM partage attache a toutes les instances

pieges.A: Gerer les permissions par utilisateur IAM individuel ne centralise rien et reste duplique
pieges.B: Des policies inline par instance = exactement le probleme actuel (duplication), pas une centralisation
pieges.D: Un groupe IAM s'associe a des utilisateurs IAM, pas a une ressource de calcul comme un notebook instance : ce mecanisme n'existe pas pour SageMaker

explication: Un notebook instance SageMaker s'execute avec un role d'execution IAM unique. En creant un seul role partage portant les permissions S3 necessaires et en l'attachant a toutes les instances de l'equipe, on centralise la gestion des acces : toute modification de permission se fait a un seul endroit et s'applique uniformement, contrairement a une gestion par utilisateur ou par policy inline individuelle.
domain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions

question: A media company streams click events from web and mobile applications into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to analyze reader behavior and generate recommendations. The analytics team needs to compute per-session metrics such as article count and dwell time using rolling 90-second windows, with near real-time latency and minimal operational overhead. Which two solutions satisfy these requirements? (Choose two)

options.A: Deploy an Amazon EMR cluster running Spark Structured Streaming to consume Kinesis events and store session aggregates in Amazon Redshift
options.B: Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to consume Kinesis Data Streams, compute rolling 90-second windowed session features, and write the results to Amazon S3
options.C: Configure Amazon OpenSearch Service to ingest data directly from Kinesis Data Streams and perform near real-time 90-second aggregations using dashboards
options.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with a Lambda transformation and a 90-second buffering interval to aggregate data before delivering it to Amazon S3
options.E: Schedule Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs to periodically read from Kinesis Data Streams and compute session-level aggregates

radar.signal: Fenetres glissantes quasi temps-reel avec peu d'ops -> services manages de streaming : Managed Service for Apache Flink et Firehose+Lambda

pieges.A: Un cluster EMR Spark Streaming = infrastructure a gerer soi-meme, contraire a 'minimal operational overhead'
pieges.C: OpenSearch ne consomme pas directement Kinesis Data Streams pour de l'agregation fenetree, il lui faut un pipeline d'ingestion en amont
pieges.E: Des jobs SageMaker Processing planifies sont du traitement par lots differe, pas du near real-time

explication: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink est concu nativement pour du traitement de flux avec fenetres temporelles (tumbling/sliding windows) en quasi temps-reel, entierement gere. Kinesis Data Firehose avec une transformation Lambda et un intervalle de buffering aligne sur 90 secondes permet aussi d'agreger avec tres peu d'operations a gerer. Les deux options evitent la gestion d'un cluster (EMR) ou un traitement par lots differe (SageMaker Processing planifie).
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: A travel company is developing a customer support application that uses Amazon Q Business to answer customer questions about travel packages. The company must ensure that responses never mention outdated or no-longer-available travel destinations. The filtering should happen before results are returned to users. Which solution best meets this requirement?

options.A: Configure Amazon Q Business blocked phrases to prevent responses that reference outdated or unavailable travel destinations
options.B: Analyze the Amazon Q Business API responses using Amazon Comprehend and suppress any responses that mention outdated destinations
options.C: Create an AWS Lambda function that post-processes Amazon Q Business responses and removes outdated destination references
options.D: Configure an Amazon Kendra retriever to exclude documents related to outdated travel destinations from the indexed content

declencheurs: filtering should happen before results are returned
radar.signal: Filtrage de contenu natif AVANT restitution -> fonctionnalite integree 'blocked phrases' de Amazon Q Business (guardrail natif)

pieges.B: Ajouter Comprehend en aval = composant supplementaire a construire/maintenir alors qu'un garde-fou natif existe deja
pieges.C: Un Lambda de post-traitement custom duplique une fonctionnalite deja native a Q Business, plus d'effort de dev
pieges.D: Exclure des documents de l'index Kendra reduit la source mais ne garantit pas que le LLM ne mentionne jamais ces destinations (connaissance parametrique, reformulations)

explication: Amazon Q Business propose une fonctionnalite native de gouvernance des reponses ('blocked phrases') permettant de bloquer directement toute reponse contenant des termes ou sujets specifiques avant qu'elle ne soit renvoyee a l'utilisateur, sans avoir a construire un pipeline de filtrage externe.
domain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions

question: A team is building a binary churn prediction model using 30-day tabular customer features in Amazon SageMaker. They want a solution that provides a fast, easy-to-set-up baseline and is simple to interpret before moving on to more complex models. Which approach best meets these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Autopilot to automatically train and tune multiple models on the dataset
options.B: Train an Amazon SageMaker XGBoost model with extensive hyperparameter optimization and 10-fold cross-validation
options.C: Apply Amazon SageMaker K-means clustering on the 30-day feature set to identify churn patterns
options.D: Train an Amazon SageMaker Linear Learner classifier using the 30-day tabular features

declencheurs: before moving on to more complex models
radar.signal: Baseline rapide et interpretable avant complexification -> Linear Learner en mode classification binaire

pieges.A: Autopilot explore plusieurs modeles automatiquement, plus lourd/long qu'une simple baseline rapide
pieges.B: HPO extensif + 10-fold CV = tres couteux en temps, l'oppose d'une baseline rapide
pieges.C: K-means est du clustering non supervise, inadapte a une tache de classification binaire supervisee

explication: SageMaker Linear Learner en mode classification binaire s'entraine rapidement, avec une configuration minimale, et produit un modele lineaire simple a interpreter (coefficients par feature), ce qui en fait la baseline ideale avant d'investir dans des modeles plus complexes comme XGBoost avec tuning extensif.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: A company is building an AI-powered fraud detection system using Amazon SageMaker. The system must support end-to-end ML workflows including data preprocessing, model training, versioned model storage, deployment, and monitoring. Transaction data is stored securely in Amazon S3, and the company requires: Secure access to training data for different workflows (data isolation). A centralized model registry to manage model versions and deployments with minimal operational overhead. Which approach best satisfies these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon S3 versioning to track model artifacts and manually manage deployments
options.B: Tag each model version uniquely and rely on SageMaker Model Registry to handle deployment logic
options.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Model Registry to centrally store model versions, group models, and manage deployments
options.D: Store all model artifacts and versions in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR)

radar.signal: Registre centralise de versions de modeles avec gestion du deploiement -> SageMaker Model Registry

pieges.A: S3 versioning suit des versions d'objets bruts, sans notion de groupe de modeles/approbation/deploiement -> gestion manuelle lourde
pieges.B: Le tagging seul ne fournit pas la logique de gestion de cycle de vie ; c'est le Model Registry lui-meme qui gere cela, pas de simples tags
pieges.D: ECR stocke des images de conteneurs, pas des artefacts/versions de modeles ML avec metadonnees de registre

explication: SageMaker Model Registry est concu specifiquement pour centraliser le versionnement des modeles, les regrouper en 'model package groups', suivre leur statut d'approbation et piloter leur deploiement, offrant une solution geree avec un minimum d'overhead operationnel, contrairement a un suivi manuel via S3 versioning, tags ou ECR.
domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows

question: A financial services company previously deployed a machine learning model using Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference with good results. Now, they need to deploy a new fraud detection model that evaluates credit card transactions in real time within their banking application. Key requirements: Real-time inference for transaction detection. Notifications whenever the model's quality deviates. The current asynchronous inference deployment does not meet the real-time performance requirements. As an AWS Certified ML Engineer Associate, which approach best addresses these requirements?

options.A: Deploy the model using SageMaker Real-Time Inference and monitor model quality using SageMaker Model Monitor
options.B: Keep SageMaker Asynchronous Inference, enable autoscaling on the endpoint, and use Amazon SQS to handle notifications
options.C: Use SageMaker Batch Transform for inference and integrate SageMaker Model Monitor for quality alerts
options.D: Increase the instance size and response timeout for the asynchronous endpoint and send quality deviation alerts via Amazon SNS

declencheurs: real time within their banking application
does not meet the real-time performance requirements
radar.signal: Detection de fraude EN TEMPS REEL + alertes de derive qualite -> SageMaker Real-Time Inference + Model Monitor

pieges.B: Rester en Asynchronous Inference ne repond toujours pas a l'exigence explicite de temps reel, quel que soit l'autoscaling
pieges.C: Batch Transform est un traitement differe par lots, incompatible avec la detection de fraude en temps reel
pieges.D: Augmenter la taille d'instance et le timeout d'un endpoint asynchrone ne le transforme pas en endpoint temps reel

explication: Seul un endpoint SageMaker Real-Time Inference garantit une reponse synchrone a faible latence necessaire pour scorer une transaction bancaire au moment de l'achat. SageMaker Model Monitor est ensuite le service dedie pour detecter toute derive de qualite du modele en production et declencher des notifications, repondant aux deux exigences simultanement.
domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows

question: A company wants to build a machine learning model to predict customer churn. The dataset includes thousands of rows with features such as customer demographics, transaction history, and support interactions, stored as CSV files in Amazon S3. The ML engineer needs to select a SageMaker built-in algorithm that: Handles tabular data. Supports supervised learning. Performs binary classification. Which algorithm is the most appropriate choice?

options.A: SageMaker Linear Learner for supervised classification on tabular data
options.B: SageMaker K-Means clustering for unsupervised grouping of customers
options.C: SageMaker XGBoost (eXtreme Gradient Boosting) for high-performance gradient-boosted trees
options.D: SageMaker BlazingText for text classification and embedding generation

radar.signal: Donnees tabulaires + classification binaire -> XGBoost, algorithme built-in de reference d'AWS pour le tabulaire

pieges.A: Linear Learner gere aussi la classification tabulaire mais offre generalement une performance inferieure a XGBoost sur ce type de donnees structurees
pieges.B: K-Means est non supervise, inadapte a une prediction binaire supervisee
pieges.D: BlazingText est concu pour du texte (NLP), pas pour des features tabulaires demographiques/transactionnelles

explication: XGBoost est l'algorithme built-in SageMaker de reference pour les donnees tabulaires structurees et offre d'excellentes performances en classification binaire supervisee (comme la prediction de churn), ce qui en fait le choix le plus approprie parmi les options proposees, devant Linear Learner qui reste une alternative plus simple mais generalement moins performante sur ce type de probleme.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: You are a data scientist at a media company that processes large volumes of video and image data to generate personalized content recommendations. The dataset is stored in Amazon S3 and includes: Tens of millions of small image files. Several terabytes of high-resolution video files. Training jobs on Amazon SageMaker require low-latency, high-throughput access and must complete quickly to keep up with the dynamic content pipeline. Which approach is most appropriate for these requirements?

options.A: Use Fast File mode with Amazon S3 to stream small image files directly to training instances on demand, reducing training startup time
options.B: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre to mount the entire dataset as a high-performance file system, providing consistently low-latency access for both images and videos
options.C: Use Fast File mode with Amazon S3 for large video files and store small image files locally on the training instances to reduce latency
options.D: Combine approaches: link small image files in FSx for Lustre and access large video files via Fast File mode from S3, leveraging the strengths of both

declencheurs: tens of millions of small image files
radar.signal: Deux profils de fichiers tres differents -> combiner FSx for Lustre (millions de petits fichiers) + S3 Fast File mode (gros fichiers volumineux)

pieges.A: Fast File mode seul est optimal pour de gros fichiers sequentiels, moins adapte a des millions de tres petits fichiers (overhead par requete S3)
pieges.B: Monter tout le dataset (y compris plusieurs TB de video) sur FSx for Lustre est possible mais plus couteux/complexe que de laisser les gros fichiers en Fast File mode direct depuis S3
pieges.C: Stocker les images localement sur les instances de training n'est pas scalable ni persistant, et perd le benefice d'un stockage partage

explication: FSx for Lustre excelle sur l'acces a tres grand nombre de petits fichiers (cache haute performance lie a S3, evite l'overhead d'un GET S3 par fichier), tandis que S3 Fast File mode est optimal pour streamer efficacement de gros fichiers volumineux directement depuis S3. Combiner les deux approches selon le type de fichier permet d'obtenir un acces a faible latence et fort debit sur l'ensemble heterogene du dataset.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: A healthcare organization is running a predictive ML model in production using Amazon SageMaker. SageMaker Model Monitor is enabled to track data quality. After a recent model update, the data scientist notices that Model Monitor flags data quality issues. What is the correct way to address these data quality issues?

options.A: Modify the model's hyperparameters and redeploy the updated model version to production
options.B: Generate a new baseline from the latest dataset and configure Model Monitor to use it for future evaluations
options.C: Ingest Amazon Ground Truth labels to create an updated baseline for future monitoring
options.D: Review the constraint_violations.json file, manually fix the current dataset, and rerun the model

radar.signal: Le modele/schema d'entree a change -> re-generer une baseline Model Monitor a jour plutot que patcher les symptomes

pieges.A: Modifier les hyperparametres n'a aucun rapport avec un desalignement entre baseline de donnees et donnees actuelles
pieges.C: Les labels Ground Truth servent a evaluer la QUALITE du modele (ModelQualityMonitor), pas la DataQualityMonitor baseline des features d'entree
pieges.D: Corriger manuellement le dataset courant est ponctuel et non reproductible ; le probleme reviendra a la prochaine ingestion

explication: Suite a une mise a jour du modele, les statistiques de reference (baseline) capturees avant deploiement peuvent ne plus correspondre a la distribution actuelle attendue des donnees d'entree, generant de fausses alertes de derive. La solution correcte est de regenerer une baseline a partir du dataset le plus recent et de reconfigurer Model Monitor pour l'utiliser comme nouvelle reference, plutot que de corriger manuellement chaque violation ponctuelle.
domain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions

question: A data scientist is training a deep neural network for image classification. They set the learning rate to 0.1, but the training loss fluctuates wildly between epochs and shows no clear improvement. What is the most likely cause of this behavior, and what action should be taken?

options.A: The learning rate is too high; they should decrease it to help the model converge smoothly
options.B: The batch size is too small; they should increase it to stabilize training
options.C: The learning rate is optimal; they should add more training data to reduce fluctuations
options.D: The learning rate is too low; they should increase it to accelerate convergence

radar.signal: Loss qui oscille violemment sans converger -> learning rate trop eleve -> le diminuer

pieges.B: La taille du batch peut influencer le bruit du gradient, mais une oscillation 'wild' avec LR=0.1 pointe d'abord vers un LR trop agressif
pieges.C: Plus de donnees n'empeche pas des pas de gradient trop grands de faire diverger l'optimisation
pieges.D: Un LR trop bas donnerait une convergence lente et reguliere, pas des oscillations violentes

explication: Un learning rate trop eleve fait 'sauter' l'optimiseur au-dela du minimum a chaque mise a jour, provoquant des oscillations importantes et persistantes de la loss sans convergence. La correction standard est de reduire le learning rate pour permettre des pas plus petits et une convergence plus stable.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: A company is running an Amazon SageMaker training job that needs to access data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. Company compliance policies require that the data must never traverse the public internet. How should the SageMaker job be configured to meet this requirement?

options.A: Launch the notebook instances in a private subnet and access S3 via a VPC endpoint
options.B: Launch the notebook instances in a public subnet and access S3 through the public endpoint
options.C: Launch the notebook instances in a public subnet and access S3 through a NAT gateway
options.D: Launch the notebook instances in a private subnet and access S3 through a NAT gateway

declencheurs: must never traverse the public internet
radar.signal: Trafic S3 qui ne doit jamais sortir sur Internet -> subnet prive + VPC Endpoint (Gateway) pour S3, trafic reste sur le reseau AWS

pieges.B: Endpoint public depuis un subnet public = trafic transite potentiellement par Internet
pieges.C: Un NAT gateway route vers Internet via l'Internet Gateway, ce qui viole l'exigence de ne jamais traverser Internet
pieges.D: Meme en subnet prive, passer par un NAT gateway fait toujours transiter le trafic par Internet pour atteindre S3

explication: Un VPC Endpoint (de type Gateway pour S3) permet d'acceder a Amazon S3 directement depuis un subnet prive via le reseau prive d'AWS, sans jamais transiter par une passerelle Internet ou un NAT gateway, ce qui est la seule option garantissant que les donnees ne traversent jamais l'Internet public.
domain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions

question: A regulated digital payments startup in North America needs to score card transactions for fraud in under 70 milliseconds during bursts of up to 180,000 requests per minute. The solution must: Protect highly sensitive user data. Maintain very high availability. Provide resilient, real-time inference at scale. Which AWS approach best satisfies these requirements?

options.A: Train and host models on Amazon SageMaker with managed auto scaling across multiple Availability Zones and protect the public interface using AWS Shield Advanced
options.B: Deploy models on AWS Lambda with Amazon Cognito for user access, leveraging serverless architecture to handle bursts
options.C: Train models using AWS Glue and deploy on Amazon ECS with manual scaling and AWS WAF protecting the service
options.D: Use Amazon EC2 for both training and hosting with manual scaling and Amazon Inspector for vulnerability assessments
options.E: Use Amazon EMR for distributed training and run inference on on-premises servers connected to AWS through a VPN

radar.signal: Inference temps reel a tres forte echelle + tres haute dispo + donnees sensibles -> SageMaker managed + autoscaling multi-AZ + Shield Advanced

pieges.B: Lambda pour de l'inference ML a tres faible latence et fort volume est risque (cold starts, limites de duree/memoire), et Cognito gere l'auth utilisateur, pas la protection DDoS de l'inference
pieges.C: Scaling manuel sur ECS ne repond pas assez vite a des pics soudains de 180k req/min ; WAF protege contre des attaques applicatives, pas contre l'indisponibilite en charge
pieges.D: EC2 avec scaling manuel ne peut pas suivre des bursts imprevisibles, et Inspector fait de l'analyse de vulnerabilites, pas de la protection en disponibilite
pieges.E: L'inference sur des serveurs on-premises via VPN ajoute de la latence reseau incompatible avec un objectif de moins de 70 ms

explication: SageMaker avec autoscaling manage sur plusieurs zones de disponibilite repond a la fois a l'exigence de tres haute disponibilite et a la capacite d'absorber des pics de charge en temps reel avec une faible latence. AWS Shield Advanced protege l'interface publique contre les attaques DDoS, ce qui est crucial pour un service de paiement expose et manipulant des donnees sensibles a fort enjeu de resilience.
domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows

question: A global e-commerce company has trained a custom sentiment analysis model in Amazon Comprehend in Account A (us-west-2). The company now needs the same model in Account B for customer feedback analysis. The solution must: Ensure secure and efficient transfer. Require minimal development effort. Which approach best meets these requirements?

options.A: Use the Amazon Comprehend ImportModel API in Account B to import the model from Account A, configuring a resource-based IAM policy in Account A
options.B: Use the Amazon Comprehend ImportModel API in Account B to import the model from Account A, configuring a resource-based IAM policy in Account B
options.C: Manually download the model artifacts from S3 in Account A and upload them to S3 in Account B, then use a custom script to recreate the model
options.D: Register the model metadata in AWS Glue Data Catalog in Account A, enable cross-account sharing, and access it from Account B via the Comprehend console

radar.signal: Copie cross-account d'un modele Comprehend -> ImportModel API + resource-based policy attachee sur la ressource SOURCE (compte A, proprietaire du modele)

pieges.B: La resource-based policy doit etre attachee dans le compte qui POSSEDE la ressource (compte A), pas dans le compte qui l'importe (compte B)
pieges.C: Les artefacts de modele Comprehend ne sont pas concus pour etre manipules/recrees manuellement via un script custom, effort et risque plus eleves
pieges.D: Le Glue Data Catalog stocke des metadonnees de donnees tabulaires, pas des modeles Comprehend ; ce mecanisme n'existe pas pour ce cas d'usage

explication: Pour partager une ressource entre comptes AWS, le compte proprietaire (Account A) doit attacher une politique basee sur les ressources (resource-based policy) autorisant Account B a y acceder. Account B appelle ensuite l'API ImportModel de Comprehend en referencant l'ARN du modele source pour en obtenir une copie, ce qui constitue le mecanisme natif, securise et a faible effort de developpement pour ce transfert cross-account.
domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows

question: An Insurance Group is deploying an omnichannel support platform for phone calls and email. The team uses Amazon Transcribe for real-time speech-to-text to power analytics and automated responses. They want to monitor error logs and key performance metrics in near real-time. Which AWS service should they integrate with Amazon Transcribe to achieve this?

options.A: Amazon S3 to store raw transcripts for later analysis
options.B: AWS Lambda to process the transcription results
options.C: AWS X-Ray to trace the application workflow
options.D: Amazon QuickSight to visualize the logs and metrics
options.E: Amazon CloudWatch to capture logs and metrics in near real-time

declencheurs: monitor error logs and key performance metrics
radar.signal: Logs d'erreurs + metriques en quasi temps-reel -> Amazon CloudWatch (Logs + Metrics + Alarms)

pieges.A: S3 stocke des transcripts pour analyse ulterieure, ce n'est pas un outil de monitoring de logs/metriques en temps reel
pieges.B: Lambda peut traiter les resultats mais ne fournit pas nativement le monitoring de logs/metriques lui-meme
pieges.C: X-Ray trace des requetes distribuees pour du debug de latence, pas specifiquement des logs d'erreur/metriques de service
pieges.D: QuickSight visualise des donnees deja collectees (souvent depuis CloudWatch), ce n'est pas la source de collecte des logs/metriques

explication: Amazon CloudWatch est le service natif d'AWS pour collecter et surveiller en quasi temps-reel les logs et metriques operationnelles d'un service comme Amazon Transcribe (CloudWatch Logs pour les erreurs, CloudWatch Metrics/Alarms pour les KPIs), avec la possibilite d'alerter automatiquement en cas d'anomalie.
domain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions

question: An e-commerce company streams real-time clickstream data from its website into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to analyze user behavior and generate product recommendations. The company wants to aggregate data at one-minute intervals to compute features such as page views and session dwell time. The solution must provide: Low-latency processing. Minimal operational overhead. Which two options best meet these requirements? (Choose two)

options.A: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
options.B: Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs
options.C: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Lambda aggregation
options.D: Amazon EMR cluster with Spark Streaming
options.E: Amazon OpenSearch Service

radar.signal: Meme pattern que l'agregation en fenetre glissante (Q33) -> services de streaming manages : Flink et Firehose+Lambda

pieges.B: SageMaker Processing planifie = traitement par lots differe, pas du near real-time
pieges.D: Cluster EMR = infrastructure a gerer, overhead operationnel eleve
pieges.E: OpenSearch n'est pas un moteur de calcul d'agregation en flux depuis Kinesis, il lui faut un pipeline d'ingestion en amont

explication: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink et Kinesis Data Firehose avec transformation Lambda sont tous deux des services entierement geres permettant d'agreger un flux Kinesis a intervalle regulier avec une faible latence et sans avoir a provisionner ou administrer d'infrastructure, contrairement a un cluster EMR ou des jobs batch planifies.
domain: Data Preparation for ML and AI

question: You are an ML engineer at a logistics company that uses machine learning models for: Delivery route optimization. Maintenance prediction. Demand forecasting. The company wants to deploy several models on the same SageMaker infrastructure to minimize costs. Models differ in update frequency. You need a deployment strategy that efficiently manages multiple models with varying update requirements. Which SageMaker deployment strategy is most suitable?

options.A: Deploy each model individually on separate SageMaker endpoints, giving each dedicated resources and independent scaling
options.B: Use a multi-container deployment on a single SageMaker endpoint, with each model in its own container to manage resources per model
options.C: Use a multi-model deployment on a single SageMaker endpoint to host all models together, dynamically loading models as needed without separate endpoints
options.D: Implement a hybrid strategy: deploy frequently updated models using multi-model endpoints and more complex models using multi-container endpoints to balance flexibility and resource management

declencheurs: several models on the same infrastructure to minimize costs
radar.signal: Plusieurs modeles, infra partagee, cout minimal, mises a jour independantes -> SageMaker Multi-Model Endpoint (MME)

pieges.A: Un endpoint dedie par modele = le plus couteux, exactement ce que l'on cherche a eviter
pieges.B: Le multi-container fixe un ensemble de conteneurs par endpoint, moins flexible qu'un MME pour ajouter/mettre a jour des modeles independamment
pieges.D: Solution hybride plus complexe a operer, alors qu'un MME seul gere deja nativement des mises a jour de modeles independantes (simple remplacement de l'artefact en S3)

explication: Un Multi-Model Endpoint SageMaker heberge plusieurs modeles sur une infrastructure partagee, les chargeant dynamiquement en memoire a la demande, ce qui minimise les couts d'infrastructure. Chaque modele peut etre mis a jour independamment en remplaçant simplement son artefact dans S3, sans redeployer l'endpoint, ce qui gere naturellement des frequences de mise a jour differentes entre modeles.
domain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows

question: A financial analytics company runs a weekly data aggregation job every Saturday night to process transactional data from the past week. The job: Runs for approximately 2 hours. Can tolerate interruptions. Will run every weekend for the next 6 months. Which EC2 instance purchasing option is the most cost-effective for this scenario?

options.A: Use EC2 Spot Instances to run the aggregation job, taking advantage of low cost and tolerating interruptions
options.B: Use EC2 Reserved Instances with a 6-month commitment to lower costs and guarantee availability
options.C: Use EC2 On-Demand Instances each weekend, paying only for the 2 hours of compute used
options.D: Use EC2 Dedicated Hosts to gain full control over infrastructure and long-term cost efficiency

radar.signal: Job court, tolerant aux interruptions, usage intermittent -> Spot Instances (remise maximale)

pieges.B: Reserver 6 mois en continu pour ~2h d'usage par semaine (environ 52h sur 6 mois) est extremement gaspilleur, on paie pour du temps inutilise
pieges.C: On-Demand fonctionne mais coute plus cher que Spot pour une charge qui tolere justement les interruptions
pieges.D: Les Dedicated Hosts sont le choix le plus couteux, totalement disproportionne pour un job de 2h hebdomadaire

explication: Le job est court, ponctuel et explicitement tolerant aux interruptions : c'est le cas d'usage ideal pour les EC2 Spot Instances, qui offrent la plus forte remise par rapport a On-Demand. Une Reserved Instance sur 6 mois serait tres inefficace puisque l'usage reel ne represente que quelques heures par semaine.
domain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions

question: A company provides personalized product recommendations for e-commerce platforms. You need a solution that can: Quickly generate high-quality product descriptions. Tailor marketing copy to customer preferences. Analyze customer reviews for sentiment trends. The solution must handle large-scale data, provide flexibility to choose foundational models, and integrate seamlessly with existing AWS infrastructure. Which AWS service best meets these requirements?

options.A: Amazon Rekognition
options.B: Amazon Personalize
options.C: Amazon Bedrock
options.D: Amazon SageMaker

radar.signal: Generation de texte + choix flexible de plusieurs Foundation Models -> Amazon Bedrock

pieges.A: Rekognition analyse des images/videos, pas de la generation de texte
pieges.B: Personalize genere des recommandations de produits, pas du texte marketing ni d'analyse de sentiment
pieges.D: SageMaker permettrait de tout construire soi-meme (plus d'effort de dev) alors que Bedrock offre deja l'acces manage a des FMs prets a l'emploi

explication: Amazon Bedrock donne acces via API a plusieurs Foundation Models de differents fournisseurs, permettant de generer rapidement des descriptions produit et du contenu marketing personnalise ainsi que d'analyser le sentiment des avis clients (prompting), tout en s'integrant nativement a l'infrastructure AWS existante, sans avoir a entrainer ou heberger soi-meme des modeles comme le necessiterait SageMaker.
domain: ML Model and FM Development

question: You are deploying a machine learning model on Amazon SageMaker. The requirements are: Production p95 latency < 30 ms. High throughput (high QPS). Keep testing costs low. Which two compute choices best meet these requirements? (Choose two)

options.A: Use SageMaker Serverless Inference for production to handle varying traffic without managing infrastructure
options.B: Use small CPU instances for the test endpoint to minimize cost
options.C: Use Inferentia-based instances for production to achieve low-latency, high-throughput inference
options.D: Use the largest GPU instance for production to guarantee the lowest latency
options.E: Use Spot capacity for both production and test endpoints to reduce cost

radar.signal: Prod = faible latence/fort debit au meilleur cout -> instances Inferentia ; Test = cout minimal -> petites instances CPU

pieges.A: Serverless Inference peut souffrir de cold starts qui compromettent un p95 strict de 30 ms
pieges.D: La plus grosse instance GPU garantit une faible latence mais au cout le plus eleve, non optimise
pieges.E: Utiliser du Spot en PRODUCTION pour un endpoint temps reel critique risque des interruptions incompatibles avec la haute disponibilite attendue

explication: Les instances basees sur AWS Inferentia sont concues pour offrir un excellent rapport latence/debit/cout pour l'inference en production, adaptees a un objectif de p95 sous 30 ms a fort volume. Pour l'environnement de test, ou la performance n'est pas critique, de petites instances CPU suffisent et minimisent les couts, repondant ainsi aux deux exigences distinctes de production et de test.
domain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
